# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** 13 to 17 years old across the novel's timeline  <sub>[v1 c28 P0](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0000), [v1 c34 P15](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c19 P38](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0038)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v1 c34 P15](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Domestic servant and handmaiden  <sub>[v1 c19 P38](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0038), [v1 c21 P12](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0012)</sub>
- **Titles:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v1 c19 P43](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0043)</sub>

## Appearance

Belinda has a freckled, small face with a snub nose, a wide mouth that stretches from ear to ear, and pale, light eyes. She wears her long, fair hair in two heavy braids fastened with massive blue ribbon bows that stick out like wings behind her head. As she grows into young womanhood, she styles her hair in a large pompadour, though her freckles, snub nose, and broad grin remain unchanged.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P38](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0038), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c25 P34](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0034), [v1 c27 P28](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0028)_

## Personality

Belinda is practical, talkative, and intensely loyal to her mistress, Miss Rosalind. She possesses an infectious, broad smile and a cheerful disposition, though she is prone to theatrical worries and dramatic fretting during stressful events. She considers herself somewhat unsuited for men and prefers domestic service, executing her tasks with great energy and devotion. She deeply admires Nell Harcourt, frequently striving to mimic her posture, speech, and graceful demeanor.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P38](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0038), [v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052), [v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070), [v1 c21 P12](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0012), [v1 c27 P27](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0027), [v1 c27 P39](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0039)_

## History

Belinda comes to work as a handmaiden for Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage at the age of thirteen. Being the fourth consecutive Bowman sister to hold the position, she is designated 'Belinda the Fourth' by her mistress. She manages the household chores, keeps Miss Rosalind's secrets, and participates in her imaginative games.

When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke visit Echo Cottage, Belinda greets them cheerfully and assists with hosting. She becomes a close confidante to Nell, admiring her greatly and attempting to imitate her mannerisms. When Stephen Stanhope arrives to woo Miss Rosalind, Belinda eagerly tracks the romance and helps prepare for the wedding. Following Miss Rosalind's marriage to Stephen Stanhope, Belinda moves with them to Boston to continue her service. Years later, she returns to Echo Cottage for summer visits, eventually marrying a American bricklayer named Tom.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P38](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0038), [v1 c19 P76](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0076), [v1 c27 P27](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0027), [v1 c27 P39](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0039), [v1 c29 P3](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0003), [v1 c34 P15](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0015), [v1 c36 P18](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0018), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038)_

## Background by volume

- Her real name is Leonora Bowman, but she is called 'Belinda the Fourth' by Miss Rosalind, who names all her young hired girls Belinda
- She is the youngest and last of the Bowman daughters from her family to serve at Echo Cottage
- Entered Miss Rosalind's service at age thirteen in exchange for board, room, and clothes

## Quotes

> I’ve been dreadfully anxious, pondering whatever would become of her once I grew so large that I must depart for Boston. No other girls remain in our family, and heaven only knows what would happen to her if she hired a stranger who could mock her imaginative play, leave items scattered out of place, and refuse to accept the name Belinda the Fifth.  <sub>[v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)</sub>

> Oh, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t.  <sub>[v1 c27 P19](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0019)</sub>

> I certainly never believed I would descend to taking a Yankee as my husband, Miss Harcourt, ma’am.  <sub>[v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038)</sub>
